summary: Early Whitfield County, GA tower near the Tennessee line; first staffed by a Crow family lookout, sold privately around 2009 and closed to the public by 2019.

facts.status_note: Standing at the February 2019 visit, which marks its condition as not good; no later condition report found.

staffing.status: not staffed (Register staffing field reads No)

access.note: Register says the site is not open to the public and no access is allowed; the road is gated twice and fenced.

visit.trail_note: Private, gated road. The 2019 visitor could not climb the tower.

events.note: Ownership passed from the state to Mrs. Crow's son, around 2009 per the Register; the timing conflicts with the Register's own sequence (see resolved_conflicts)
Visit report dated February 8, 2019: needs paint, wood and stairs not OK, not maintained for safety, not open to the public

evidence.supports: location less than five miles from the Tennessee line; early fire tower
evidence.quote: This early fire tower is located in extreme northern Georgia, less than five miles from the Tennessee state line.

evidence.supports: first staffed by Mrs. Crow, whose family owned the land
evidence.quote: this tower was originally staffed by Mrs. Crow, whose family owned the land where the tower is located

evidence.supports: served 36 years as the lookout at the tower
evidence.quote: served 36 years as the lookout at the McGaughey's forestry tower

evidence.supports: first female lookout for the Commission in Georgia
evidence.quote: first female lookout for the Commission in the state of Georgia

evidence.supports: lease ended and tower set for removal
evidence.quote: Sometime after her death, and the end of the Georgia Forestry Commission's lease of the land, the tower was scheduled for removal.

evidence.supports: son bought the tower from the state around 2009
evidence.quote: Mrs. Crow's son purchased the tower from the state around 2009

evidence.supports: obituary records her death in October 2016
2019 visit: privately bought about ten years earlier; not maintained for safety; not open to public
evidence.quote: The tower was privately purchased approx 10 years ago, and is no longer maintained for safety; nor accessible to the public.
The road is gated twice, and fenced.

evidence.supports: visitor could not climb the tower
owned by the son's widow as of 2019
evidence.quote: As of 2019, the tower is now owned by his widow.

evidence.supports: not open to the public; no access allowed
evidence.quote: This tower and its site are not open to the public.

evidence.supports: administered by a private owner, previously the Commission

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register dates the sale to Mrs. Crow's son to around 2009 but places it after her death, while the obituary records her death in October 2016. The event keeps the Register's around-2009 date and flags the conflict; the story says the sources do not reconcile it.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. No build year, design or height appears in any source read. The obituary is used only for the lookout role and the death date; the story does not repeat her name. The NHLR photo credit (Justin Peel) has no image URL, so no photo entry. The latest report is the February 2019 visit; the Register's staffing field is undated. Brief's access 'unknown' is updated to private.
